# Cave pickup PNG assets

## animal-bone-pixel-v1.png

Final style reference: bone-fragment-pixel-v1.png. Earlier opaque variants were discarded.

Use this transparent pixel art bone fragment as reference to make a COMPLETE animal long bone pickup sprite in precisely the same style and palette. The complete bone must have two rounded knobby joint ends joined by a narrow gently curved shaft, diagonal lower-left to upper-right. Center it with a small clear margin. One dry ivory bone only. Deliver on a TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND with actual alpha transparency, exactly like this reference's transparent exterior. Compact retro JRPG pixel art item, readable at 36 pixels, dark brown outline, cream highlights, warm gray shadows. No ground or cast shadow.

Generated with the built-in image_gen tool. Original PNG outputs are preserved; the game renders them with nearest-neighbor filtering. Initial style references: `../beach-shell-v1.png` and `../../tiles/forest/rocks/jungle-rock-large-v1.png`.

## bone-fragment-pixel-v1.png

Create ONE production PNG pickup-item sprite for PETOA retro JRPG. Attached seashell item and rock are STYLE REFERENCES: match their crisp hand-crafted pixel art, dark selective outline, limited nuanced palette, top-left highlights and compact top-down/three-quarter view. Subject: one short BROKEN fragment of animal bone, irregular jagged broken ends exposing a darker hollow center, ivory and warm gray, unmistakably a broken fragment rather than a complete long bone, dry and clean, no flesh. Composition: short squat irregular silhouette, centered, subject occupies 80% of square canvas, no other objects. This will display at roughly 32x32 game pixels: design deliberate readable pixel clusters and stepped edges, as a native 32x32 sprite enlarged nearest-neighbor. Actual transparent alpha background everywhere outside the object, no colored backdrop, no checkerboard artwork, no ground tile, no pedestal, no labels, no text. A tiny close contact shadow is okay but no broad diffuse cast shadow. Not vector clipart, not smooth 3D, not photorealistic. Exactly one item.

## blue-shard-pixel-v1.png

Generated with the built-in `image_gen` tool on 2026-09-14. Original PNG and transparent alpha preserved. Three instances reuse the sprite at different angles in the blue rock chamber. The game uses nearest-neighbor filtering.

Final prompt:

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single collectible item sprite for a retro top-down 16-bit Japanese RPG cave. Create ONE small irregular broken fragment of blue glowing bedrock, centered alone, fully visible with generous transparent padding on all sides. Genuine transparent alpha background. Chunky, crisp pixel art: approximately 32x32 logical pixels, nearest-neighbor enlarged, limited palette of deep navy outlines, dark cobalt stone faces, bright cyan mineral veins and a few pale icy-blue square highlights. It should look like a broken angular stone chip, not a polished jewel, not a cluster of crystals. Three copies of this sprite will be placed on a cave floor at 40px display size. Slight top-down three-quarter view. No floor, no ground shadow, no text, no border, no props, no smooth gradients, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no soft glow outside the silhouette.
